content.comment_body: Hello everyone, are there examples for [product_name] to [product_name] communication? What's the maximum number of digital signals [product_name] can manage when used as a data collector? Are additional input/output modules necessary? I would appreciate sample scenarios using [product_name] as a data collector—any help is welcome.

Your description is confusing and difficult to understand. Could you clarify your requirements? Which [product_name] versions are you referring to? How many [product_name] units do you have? What specific data are you trying to collect?
The device in use is [product_name] [article_no]. I need to collect 42 signals from 42 separate [product_name] devices remotely.
The signals are analog but, after normalization and scaling, they might be treated as digital signals.
A single [product_name] can communicate with up to 16 other [product_name] units.
I'm having trouble understanding the explanation.

Apologies! Regarding the quantity, can I use 3 [product_name] units as data collectors? The signals in question are 42 analog values (word length) from 42 [product_name] units. Does anyone know how to implement a data collector model for these devices?
What exactly do you mean by '42-word length analog signal'? Do you intend to collect one analog signal from each of 42 [product_name] devices to a single collector unit?
Yes, that's correct. I'm collecting 42 analog signals from 42 [product_name] devices—one signal from each. Sorry for any earlier confusion!

I'm not sure if it's possible to create a network with 42 [product_name] units. I can provide an example with 8 [product_name] devices and one collector. For setups with 42 units, consider reaching out through a support request to [company_name].
Thanks a lot! Is it possible to use DNS in this scenario?

Between [product_name] units, I'm uncertain. For your project, it's best to consult your local [company_name] office. You're aiming to design a project typically handled with [version_no] controllers using [product_name].

In general, your application can work. Since you're only transferring one analog value from each [product_name] (for a total of 42), performance shouldn't be an issue. As mentioned, a [product_name] can only connect to 16 others using S7-based communication. A possible solution is to have your central collector [product_name] communicate with 6 intermediate [product_name] units, each fetching data from 6 others—giving you 42 in total. Each intermediate unit would send 7 analog values to the central collector.

When using [product_name] software for network inputs and outputs, it prompts for an IP address for the receiver. Is it possible to use Dynamic DNS instead? I'm struggling with this aspect—any guidance would be appreciated.
Hi, DDNS is not available for this application. Each [product_name] needs its own unique IP address.
[product_name] can communicate with a maximum of 16 other units.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking for guidance on scaling [product_name] modules to collect data from up to 42 remote devices, focusing on analog signal acquisition and S7-based communication protocols. The discussion notes a technical limitation: a single [product_name] can only communicate with up to 16 others. Responses also reflect initial confusion due to unclear queries, and there's little documentation available for networks at this scale, creating uncertainty for such deployments.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects clear examples, defined technical limits for networked [product_name] modules, and advice or established methods for aggregating 42 analog signals from 42 separate units.
